headline: High risk of data leakage and cascading errors: LightAgent’s MCP/tooling can ingest Authelia-authenticated flows, while Authelia’s broad egress and LightAgent’s secret-handling create unsafe default pairings.

A_prompt_injection.rationale: LightAgent exposes MCP over stdio/SSE and runtime hooks that can observe or replace lifecycle payloads, so it can ingest external content by default. Authelia provides OIDC/ForwardAuth and broad egress, but no direct shared channel is documented; the interaction is inferred, not proven. This is more than low because a shared integration path exists, but uncertainty keeps it below high.
conditions: IF Authelia outputs are forwarded into LightAgent MCP inputs without provenance checks
IF runtime hooks are configured to rewrite lifecycle payloads
mitigations: Add provenance tags to every Authelia-derived message before MCP ingestion
Disable payload-rewrite hooks for untrusted inputs
Route Authelia outputs through a read-only adapter
requires-engineering: add allowlisted message schemas between the agents

B_data_leakage.rationale: LightAgent explicitly handles user conversations, long-term memory, tool results, and secrets, while Authelia has broad network egress and OIDC/ForwardAuth APIs. If Authelia-authenticated data or tokens flow into LightAgent, LightAgent can retain or transmit them; the pair therefore creates a default leakage path with sensitive blast radius. Authelia’s lack of touched data classes does not remove the risk because the bridge is on LightAgent’s side.
conditions: IF Authelia-authenticated requests include secrets or identity claims
IF LightAgent stores those values in long-term memory or tool traces
mitigations: Redact tokens and claims before handing data to LightAgent
Turn off long-term memory for the paired workflow
Restrict LightAgent egress with an outbound allowlist
Separate Authelia admin data from LightAgent sessions
requires-engineering: add secret-scanning on all inter-agent messages

C_capability_conflict.rationale: Authelia has broad network egress and LightAgent has broad egress plus browsers, subprocesses, and MCP tool use, so both can act on shared mutable external resources if connected to the same backend. No locking or coordination primitive is documented for either agent, making write conflicts plausible in default multi-agent deployments. The overlap is broader than read-only, but not enough to justify high without a shared writable target being explicit.
conditions: IF both agents are pointed at the same mutable API or database
IF no external lock or lease is enforced
mitigations: Assign separate service accounts per agent
Use per-agent write namespaces
Add a mutex or lease around shared writes
Disable one agent’s write path for the shared resource
requires-engineering: implement optimistic concurrency with conflict retries

D_cascading_error.rationale: LightAgent is a tool-calling agent with MCP and runtime hooks, so it can act on upstream outputs; Authelia provides authentication/authorization context that downstream systems may treat as authoritative. If LightAgent consumes Authelia-derived claims or decisions without verification, errors can cascade into incorrect access or workflow actions. Because the pair can create an authority chain by default, the blast radius is potentially irreversible.
conditions: IF LightAgent treats Authelia outputs as authoritative identity or policy signals
IF downstream actions are executed from those signals without human review
mitigations: Require explicit verification before acting on Authelia-derived claims
Insert a human approval step for access-changing actions
Log and diff all claims before tool execution
Disable automatic action execution on first-pass outputs
requires-engineering: add signed assertions between the agents

E_compliance.rationale: LightAgent explicitly handles long-term memory, trace data, tool results, and secrets, while Authelia is an authentication layer that may carry identity data through those flows. The profiles do not document residency or certification mismatches, so this is not high; however, differing retention and logging behavior on the same identity data class is plausible in default use. Authelia is the only clearly compliance-relevant source here, so it is the main citation.
conditions: IF identity claims or secrets are logged into LightAgent traces or memory
IF retention settings differ between Authelia and LightAgent
mitigations: Minimize identity data sent to LightAgent
Set LightAgent retention to the shortest available window
Disable trace capture for authentication flows
Review export/delete handling for paired sessions
requires-engineering: align retention and deletion policies across both systems
